cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Make It Their Idea
cards.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've outgrown the tool drawer I taught you to organize. Sorting this shed could give you a whole workshop of your own.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Until you dump paint tins over everything again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the final lesson: make the teacher obey the labels. You could set every shelf's rules.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Including one you're forbidden to touch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Especially that one. Put it at eye level so I have to admire how thoroughly you've learned to keep me out.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 graduation from taught drawer to own workshop sells sorting; A3 calls forcing teacher compliance the final lesson; A5 treats B4 exclusion rule as proof of successful training and makes it visible.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 paint dumping causes A3 rule authority; B4 forbidden shelf tests that authority and A5 affirms a conspicuous ban.

relationship.evidence: B4 demands a real limit on A's habitual intrusion.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4 power over the teacher the most appealing part of the unwanted sorting job.

specificity.evidence: A1 shed/tools and B2 tins anchor the repeated nuisance; B4 shelf creates a specific territory.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 eye-level admiration makes the concession tempting without an abstract promise of empowerment.
